name: Autosomal Dominant Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes Due to Defective Synaptic Vesicles Exocytosis
aliases: AD CMS with Synaptic Vesicle Exocytosis Defect
Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome Type Synaptic Vesicle Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with onset in infancy or early childhood
Electrophysiological evidence of impaired neuromuscular transmission including decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in synaptic vesicle exocytosis (e.g., SYT2, SNAP25)
Clinical improvement with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or 3,4-diaminopyridine

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect plus pathogenic genetic variant in synaptic vesicle exocytosis gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is critical due to phenotypic overlap with other CMS subtypes.

pathognomonic.notes: Worsens with exertion and improves with rest
searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use

pathognomonic.symptomName: Oculobulbar weakness with ptosis and ophthalmoparesis
searchTerms: drooping eyelids and eye muscle weakness
weakness of eye and throat muscles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Impaired synaptic vesicle exocytosis confirmed by genetic mutation
searchTerms: genetic defect causing nerve signal release problems

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to bulbar muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to throat muscle weakness

common.notes: May lead to respiratory insufficiency during crises
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

common.notes: Early muscle fatigue on minimal exertion

occasional.notes: Slurred speech due to bulbar weakness

imaging: Normal brain and spinal cord MRI
Possible mild muscle atrophy on muscle MRI
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SYT2, SNAP25, or other synaptic vesicle exocytosis genes
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Different gene mutations affecting postsynaptic or presynaptic proteins
Autoimmune etiology with anti-acetylcholine receptor or anti-MuSK antibodies
Fluctuating weakness with immunosuppressive treatment response

redFlags: Rapid progression of muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Failure to respond to standard acetylcholinesterase inhibitor therapy
Presence of autonomic dysfunction or cardiac arrhythmias
